title: Highest-Protein Nuts: Ranking per 100 Grams and per Ounce

seo.title: Highest-Protein Nuts per Serving
seo.meta_description: Compare almonds, pistachios, cashews, walnuts and hazelnuts by protein per 100 grams and per 1-ounce serving, plus peanuts for context.
seo.search_intent: Compare nuts by protein concentration and realistic serving.

excerpt: Almonds and pistachios are among the highest-protein tree nuts at about 21.2 and 20.2 g per 100 g. A 1-ounce serving provides roughly 6 g.
content_html:
Nuts provide protein, fiber, minerals and mostly unsaturated fat, but per-100-gram numbers can overstate their practical protein contribution because a normal serving is about 1 ounce / 28 g.

Protein ranking

NutProtein/100 gProtein/1 oz
Almonds21.2 g5.9 g
Pistachios20.2 g5.7 g
Cashews18.2 g5.1 g
Walnuts15.2 g4.3 g
Hazelnuts15.0 g4.2 g
Brazil nuts14.3 g4.0 g
Pecans9.2 g2.6 g
Macadamias7.9 g2.2 g

Almonds and pistachios

Almonds contain about 21.2 g protein/100 g and pistachios 20.2 g. In a 1-ounce serving that becomes about 5.9 versus 5.7 g — effectively the same contribution.

Almonds also provide roughly 12.5 g fiber/100 g and substantial vitamin E; pistachios provide around 10 g fiber and are notable for vitamin B6 and potassium.

Cashews

Cashews provide about 18.2 g protein/100 g, or just over 5 g per ounce, along with copper, magnesium and zinc.

Walnuts and hazelnuts

Both are around 15 g protein/100 g and about 4 g per ounce. Walnuts are distinctive for alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), a plant omega-3, while hazelnuts are rich in vitamin E and monounsaturated fat.

Pecans and macadamias

Pecans and macadamias are lower in protein at roughly 9.2 and 7.9 g/100 g. One ounce of macadamias provides only about 2.2 g protein compared with almost 6 g from almonds.

What about peanuts?

Peanuts provide about 25.8 g protein/100 g, higher than almonds or pistachios, but botanically they are legumes. A 1-ounce serving contains about 7.2 g protein.

Protein versus calories

Nuts generally contain 550 to more than 700 calories/100 g. Almonds are around 579 calories with 21.2 g protein, while cooked chicken breast is around 165 calories with 31 g protein. Getting 30 g protein from almonds would take about 5 ounces / 142 g and more than 800 calories; chicken would require roughly 3.4 ounces / 97 g and about 160 calories.

Nuts remain valuable for unsaturated fat, fiber and micronutrients. They simply are not lean protein foods.

Raw or roasted

Roasting changes moisture slightly. Added salt, sugar, honey, chocolate or oils usually have a larger nutritional impact than the roasting itself.

Bottom line

Almonds and pistachios are the highest-protein common tree nuts. An ounce provides roughly 6 g, making nuts a useful protein addition rather than the most efficient main protein source.

Sources

Values come from USDA FoodData Central.

faq.question: Which nut has the most protein?
faq.answer: Among common tree nuts, almonds are about 21.2 g/100 g and pistachios 20.2 g/100 g.

faq.question: How much protein is in an ounce of nuts?
faq.answer: About 5.9 g in almonds, 5.7 g in pistachios, 5.1 g in cashews and 4.3 g in walnuts.

faq.question: Are peanuts higher in protein?
faq.answer: Yes, about 25.8 g/100 g, but peanuts are botanically legumes.
